submissions.findingTextShort: A 29-day Cognitaven green-oat trial reported selected cognition and physiological stress-response signals in healthy adults.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 32485993 randomized 132 healthy adults aged 35 to 65 years to several doses of a proprietary Avena sativa green-oat extract (Cognitaven) or placebo for 29 days. Selected working-memory and multitasking outcomes improved at specific doses, and the highest dose reduced electrodermal response to a laboratory stressor, while mood showed no treatment-related effect. These findings belong to the studied green-oat extract and cannot be inherited by milky-oat tincture, generic oat straw, food oats, or every preparation of Avena sativa.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy adults aged 35 to 65 years in a 29-day dose-ranging randomized trial
submissions.usageContext: Proprietary green-oat extract Cognitaven; not generic oat straw or milky-oat tincture
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Signals were outcome- and dose-specific, the treatment period was short, and mood outcomes were null.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 12-week wild-green-oat extract crossover RCT found no chronic cognitive benefit in older adults with normal cognition.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 22690320 studied Neuravena wild green oat extract at 1500 mg/day in a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial of 37 older adults with normal cognition. After 12 weeks, chronic supplementation did not affect the measured cognitive outcomes. This longer-duration null result must remain visible beside shorter acute or short-term positive signals and cannot be erased by pooling all oat-extract exposures together.
submissions.populationContext: Older adults with normal cognition in a 12-week crossover trial
submissions.usageContext: Neuravena wild-green-oat extract; chronic cognition endpoint
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The small sample limits precision, but the chronic null result is directly relevant to claims that short-term signals persist with sustained use.

submissions.findingTextShort: A systematic review found more favorable acute or short-term oat-extract signals than long-term chronic evidence.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 36657906 systematically reviewed six randomized trials involving 287 healthy participants and concluded that acute Avena sativa extract studies were generally more favorable, short-term chronic supplementation showed some improvement, and long-term chronic supplementation did not. The review rated the evidence as average quality and emphasized the small trial count and heterogeneous doses, supporting a duration-sensitive and preparation-sensitive evidence summary rather than a generic cognition claim.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy participants across six randomized Avena sativa extract trials
submissions.usageContext: Evidence synthesis across heterogeneous oat-extract preparations and durations
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Only six RCTs were included, intervention doses varied, and acute, short-term and longer chronic results were not interchangeable.
